page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, providing a total of 8 vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 446 GB SSD, and it operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate that the ecs.i1.2xlarge delivers mixed performance characteristics. In CPU-centric evaluations, the instance achieves a Passmark CPU score of 6992.14 and a Passmark CPU extended instructions test score of 5859.32, both falling within the average range. However, its stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performances are positioned in the bottom 25%. Memory performance shows a similar trend, with a weak read-only large block bandwidth of 38.77 GB/sec but an average write large block bandwidth of 35.61 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks are relatively slow, as evidenced by a weak Passmark CPU encryption score of 2720.69 and a poor single-threaded gzip compression rate of 18.95 GB/sec.

The instance demonstrates average capability in specific database and inference tasks, achieving 5.89 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and average prompt processing speeds for small 135M LLM models. Conversely, it struggles with larger models, showing poor performance on 7B LLM inference. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and integrated 446 GB local SSD, the ecs.i1.2xlarge offers a balanced resource profile for workloads requiring local storage and moderate compute density, such as small-scale databases, basic web serving, and general-purpose applications, though it presents performance tradeoffs in highly parallelized or memory-intensive operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated physical cores (8 vCPUs), 32.0 GB of RAM, and a 446 GB local SSD. Operating on a KVM hypervisor, the instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Benchmark data shows average performance in Passmark CPU tests and Redis SET operations, alongside average prompt processing for small LLM models. However, it exhibits weaker performance in stress-ng CPU tests, memory read bandwidth, and larger LLM inference tasks. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU cores and local SSD storage, such as moderate database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose applications, while presenting performance tradeoffs in memory-intensive and high-compute scenarios.
